NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION)
To prevent micro-slip fretting corrosion in EV battery pack busbar-to-cell-tab bolted joints under road vibration, we propose replacing the standard bolted joint with a spring-energized conductive washer system. Standard practice uses static preload bolts alone, which cannot compensate for vibration-induced relaxation. Our intervention introduces dynamic preload maintenance through spring washers that continuously compensate for vibration-induced dimensional changes, maintaining consistent contact pressure. This differs from existing vibration-resistant fasteners (adjacent-technique clearance) by combining spring-loaded preload maintenance with conductive material properties, addressing both mechanical relaxation and electrical contact simultaneously. The spring mechanism directly counteracts the vibration-induced micro-slip that drives fretting corrosion.

PHYSICS CHECK
The governing relation is contact pressure maintenance: P = F/A, where P is contact pressure, F is clamping force, and A is contact area. Vibration causes F to fluctuate, leading to periods where F < μN (normal force required to prevent slip), causing micro-slip. Spring-energized washers maintain F by extending/contracting with vibration, keeping F > μN continuously. The spring constant (k) is chosen such that ΔF = k·Δx > ΔF_vibration, where ΔF_vibration is the force fluctuation from vibration. For typical EV busbar joints (F = 5-10 kN, ΔF_vibration ≈ 1 kN at 20 Hz), a spring constant of 50-100 N/μm maintains F within 5% of nominal, preventing micro-slip.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL
Standard practice components:
- Bolts (M6, class 10.9)
- Busbar contact surface (aluminum)
- Cell tab contact surface (copper)
- Torque specification: 8 Nm

Intervention components:
- Bolts (M6, class 10.9) [a] - existing component retained
- Spring-energized conductive washer (Belleville spring with silver-plated contact surface) [b] - procurable standard catalog item
- Torque specification: 8 Nm [c] - parameter change (same torque, but with washer system)

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)
- Bolts: Same count and specification (no change)
- Washers: Addition of one spring washer per bolt, but replaces standard flat washer (same quantity class)
- Torque specification: Same value, same application procedure
- Installation procedure: Same torque wrench, same sequence, same torque value
- Burden class: Same (no additional tooling, no new training, no inventory complexity beyond standard washer substitution)

EXECUTABLE TEST
Protocol: Mount 20 busbar-cell-tab joints with spring-energized washers and 20 control joints with standard washers on vibration tables. Apply 20 Hz sinusoidal vibration (5g amplitude) for 1000 hours. Monitor contact resistance at 1-hour intervals using 4-wire Kelvin method (1 mA test current). Measure joint torque before and after testing. Pass/fail criterion: Intervention group shows <10% contact resistance drift vs. >15% in control group. Kill criterion: Any joint showing >20% resistance drift or visible corrosion. Duration: 1000 hours continuous vibration. Validation: Statistical significance (p<0.05) in resistance drift reduction between groups.
